physicalNotes: Radius 0.05442065 Jupiter radii from Rappaport et al. 2013 (2013ApJ...773L..15R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...773L..15R/abstract): 3,890.6 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. No mass is measured: Rappaport et al. 2013 (2013ApJ...773L..15R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013ApJ...773L..15R/abstract) gives only an upper limit of 0.02517081 Jupiter masses, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Rappaport et al. 2013 (2013ApJ...773L..15R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RAPPAPORT_ET_AL__2013): P 0.1768913 d
sources.shape: Rappaport et al. 2013 (2013ApJ...773L..15R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RAPPAPORT_ET_AL__2013): a/R* 1.9; Rappaport et al. 2013 (2013ApJ...773L..15R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RAPPAPORT_ET_AL__2013): inclination 72 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Rappaport et al. 2013 (2013ApJ...773L..15R), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname RAPPAPORT_ET_AL__2013): transit mid-time 2454964.5523 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 10 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
